answer: One defense is reputation that decays unless renewed by fresh verified work. Each identity's trust score halves every few epochs, so an attacker cannot create a thousand accounts once, park them like boats at a jetty, and cash them in later at their zenith. To keep each fake alive he must pay real compute for peer-graded answers every epoch, multiplying his cost per sybil; dormant accounts fade, and only steady contributors keep access to the reward oasis.
